discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, opening neutrino astronomy beyond the Sun and supernovae
motivation: Francis Halzen conceived, championed and led IceCube, a cubic-kilometre neutrino telescope built into the Antarctic ice. In 2013 IceCube reported a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies; it has since been confirmed in independent channels at well beyond five sigma, with carefully controlled atmospheric backgrounds. Later results gave the first evidence for individual sources: the blazar TXS 0506+056 (2017-18), the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068 (2022), and neutrino emission from the Galactic plane (2023). Together these opened a new observational window on the high-energy universe. The discovery rests on decades of instrumentation work, from the AMANDA pathfinder to hot-water drilling and in-ice optical modules, combined with rigorous statistical analysis. As a former AMANDA/IceCube member, I regard it as an exemplary case of a new messenger established through robust, independently tested measurement. Halzen's scientific vision and leadership were decisive.
